maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
I think this is too short so it becomes unclear that it's environment variable and what the default is.

Let's take more inspiration from the text about `-a <password>` and `CLI_AUTH_ENV` below.

Idea: *Server hostname or IP (default is 127.0.0.1). You can also use the xxxxx environment variable.*

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body:
The default width of a terminal window is 80 colums, so let's keep the output formatted to that width.

```suggestion
            "  -h <hostname>      Server hostname. Default is 127.0.0.1, you can also use the\n"
            "                     " CLI_HOST_ENV " environment variable.\n"
            "  -p <port>          Server port. Default is 6379, you can also use the\n"
            "                     " CLI_PORT_ENV " environment variable.\n"
```

maintainer_comments.author: enjoy-binbin
maintainer_comments.body:
We can add these lines just like -a i guess.
```
            "  -a <password>      Password to use when connecting to the server.\n"
            "                     You can also use the " CLI_AUTH_ENV " environment\n"
            "                     variable to pass this password more safely\n"
            "                     (if both are used, this argument takes precedence).\n"
```

```suggestion
            "  -h <hostname>      Server hostname (default: 127.0.0.1).\n"

maintainer_comments.author: zuiderkwast
maintainer_comments.body: I agree with you @Dietr1ch, for AUTH it can be useful to prevent the password from being store in the shell's history file, but this doesn't seem like a valid point for hostname and port.
